# Accessibility remediation (WCAG 2.1 AA / EAA) for maison-lumiere.fr

Branch `a11y/eaa-remediation-2026-10-15` → `main` (repo `maison-lumiere/storefront`)

## Summary

- **Accessibility score: 38 → 97.** EAA status: partially compliant.
- **16 of 17 issues fixed and verified (validated).** 1 issue is escalated to a human (A16).
- axe violations: 34 → 5. Keyboard-unreachable controls: 8 → 0. Elements with visible focus: 0/57 → 64/65.
- Pages covered: `/`, `/product.html`, `/cart.html`, `/checkout.html`.

## Fixes by WCAG criterion

### 1.1.1 Non-text Content (Level A)
- **A04** Cart product images had no alt text. They are decorative (the name is in the adjacent cell), so they now have `alt=""`. Commit `1036379`.
- **A11** Product photo had `alt="image"`. It is now `alt="Baskets en cuir"`. Commit `1036379`.

### 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (Level A)
- **A14** No main heading and skipped levels. The hero is now `h1` and the product cards `h2`. CSS selectors were updated so the visuals are unchanged. Commit `7f7f737`.

### 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) (Level AA)
- **A01** `.price-note` is now `#767676` (4.54:1 on white). Footer text and links are now `#595959` (about 6.3:1 on `#f7f5f2`). Backgrounds are unchanged. Commit `095222e`.

### 2.1.1 Keyboard (Level A)
All four fixes are in commit `6d3b239`.
- **A05** Size choices are now native buttons, with `aria-pressed` kept in sync by `selectSize`.
- **A06** "Payer" is now a native button.
- **A07** "Add to cart" is now a native button.
- **A08** "Commander" is now a native button.

### 2.4.2 Page Titled (Level A)
- **A17** The checkout title is now "Paiement — Maison Lumière", matching the other pages. Commit `28815ff`.

### 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context) (Level A)
- **A13** Each "En savoir plus" link has an `aria-label` that starts with the visible text and adds the product name. Commit `a00bf16`.

### 2.4.7 Focus Visible (Level AA)
- **A02** The global `*:focus { outline: none; }` was replaced with a visible 3px blue `:focus-visible` outline. Commit `e94c22e`.

### 3.1.1 Language of Page (Level A)
- **A03** `lang="fr"` was added to the `html` element of `index.html`, matching the other pages. Commit `089c44e`.

### 3.3.1 Error Identification (Level A)
- **A15** The email error is no longer shown by colour only. It now has visible error text linked with `aria-describedby`, `aria-invalid="true"`, an accessible name on the input, and a compliant red text style. Commit `c841751`.

### 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions (Level A)
- **A12** Each delivery field now has a visible `<label for>` and `autocomplete` tokens, plus a shared label style. Placeholders are kept. Commit `0dd0685`.

### 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A)
All fixes are in commit `b669310`.
- **A09** Header icon buttons were named only by emoji. The emoji are now hidden from assistive technology. Search and favorites have `aria-label`s. The cart button name is a visually-hidden "Panier" plus the visible count, so the name contains the visible text (2.5.3) and stays correct as the count changes.
- **A10** On the cart page, the remove buttons have `aria-label="Supprimer l'article"` with the emoji hidden. The header buttons are fixed as in A09.

## Needs human review

| Issue | Problem | Action required | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A16** (WCAG 1.3.1, `/checkout.html`, major) | The card payment iframe cannot be verified. It is PayVite's third-party widget, so the shop cannot safely change it. | PayVite must supply a version with real `<label>`s (or `aria-label`s) and `autocomplete` attributes (`cc-number`, `cc-exp`, `cc-csc`) on the inputs. The shop team should then embed that version with a descriptive iframe title such as "Paiement par carte bancaire". | PayVite (vendor), then the shop team |

## How this was verified

- Each page was scanned with axe-core (WCAG 2.1 A/AA rules) before and after the changes. Violations went from 34 to 5.
- A keyboard walk of each page checked focus order, accessible names, visible focus and unreachable controls. Unreachable controls went from 8 to 0, and visible focus from 0/57 to 64/65.
- AI agent review found the issues that automated tools cannot detect. These were alt text quality, labels, link purpose, headings, error identification and the third-party iframe.
- Each fix was re-checked against the baseline and accepted (status "validated"). A09 and A10 needed a second attempt. The other fixes passed on the first.
- Automated and agent checks do not replace a manual audit with assistive technology users.

# Accessibility Statement — maison-lumiere.fr

*Draft for review. Date of this statement: 15 October 2026.*

Maison Lumière is committed to making its website accessible in line with the European Accessibility Act (EAA). This statement covers maison-lumiere.fr: the home page, product page, cart and checkout.

## Compliance status

This website is **partially compliant** with WCAG 2.1 level AA and EN 301 549, because of the exceptions listed below.

## Non-accessible content

- **Card payment form (checkout).** The card fields are a third-party widget supplied by PayVite. The inputs may lack proper labels and autocomplete attributes (WCAG 1.3.1), and the widget could not be verified. We have asked the provider for a compliant version. Once it is available, we will embed it with a descriptive iframe title.
- **Remaining automated findings.** The latest automated scan still reports 5 violations. These are not itemised in the remediation record and need review.
- **Visible focus.** Keyboard focus is now visible on 64 of 65 tested elements. The one remaining element should be identified and corrected.

## Improvements already made

The following issues were corrected in October 2026:

- Keyboard access to size selection, "Add to cart", "Commander" and "Payer".
- Visible keyboard focus.
- Text contrast.
- Page language.
- Alternative text for images.
- Accessible names for icon buttons.
- Labels on delivery fields.
- Error identification for the email field.
- Heading structure.
- Descriptive link text.
- Page titles.

## How this was assessed

The assessment was a self-assessment on 15 October 2026, against WCAG 2.1 level AA and EN 301 549 (the technical standard behind the EAA). It combined:

- **Automated testing** with axe-core (WCAG 2.1 A/AA rules).
- **Automated keyboard testing** of focus order, accessible names and visible focus.
- **AI agent review** of the pages for issues that automated tools miss.

The pages tested were the home page, product page, cart and checkout. The assessment has not yet been confirmed by a manual audit with assistive technologies or by an independent party.

## Feedback and contact

If you cannot access any content or service, please contact us:

- Contact name / service: [TO COMPLETE]
- Email: [TO COMPLETE]
- Phone / postal address: [TO COMPLETE]
- Response time commitment: [TO COMPLETE]

## Enforcement procedure

If you are not satisfied with our response, you may contact the competent national enforcement authority: [TO COMPLETE — authority name, address, website and contact details].
